title: habitat component contract
description: The machine-readable contract every habitat component must satisfy. Each field exists because an agent needs it to use the component without guessing. Fields map one-to-one to the checks in agent-ready.

name.description: Canonical name plus any aliases, so the same component is referred to consistently. Maps to agent-ready: naming consistency.

aliases.description: Other names this has been called, to be normalised to the canonical name.

purpose.description: Why this component exists and what job it does, described by purpose not appearance. 'Lets a user commit to an action' not 'a rounded rectangle with a label'. Maps to agent-ready: description coverage and quality.

props.description: Every prop the agent can set, fully typed. Maps to agent-ready: component properties.

variants.description: Named variants and, crucially, WHEN to use each. Maps to agent-ready: component coverage and description quality.

whenToUse.description: The decision rule the agent should apply to pick this variant.

states.description: The interaction and status states the component must define. An agent that cannot see a state will not build it. Maps to agent-ready: state completeness.

name.description: e.g. default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading.

tokens.description: Which design token is bound to which visual property. Binding, not mere existence, is what an agent can act on. Maps to agent-ready: token binding.

relationships.description: Where this component lives and what it works with, so the agent places it correctly. Maps to agent-ready: relationships and hierarchy.

antiPatterns.description: Explicit refusals: what the agent must never do with this component. This is the conscience the agent cannot infer on its own. Maps to agent-ready: the refusals that keep generated UI honest.

never.description: The forbidden action, e.g. 'place two primary buttons in the same view'.

because.description: The reason, so the rule survives paraphrase.

accessibility.description: How the component behaves for assistive technology and keyboards. Maps to agent-ready: accessibility annotations.

keyboard.description: Key interactions, e.g. 'Enter and Space activate'.

focus.description: Focus behaviour and visible focus treatment.

content.description: Real example content, never lorem ipsum, so the agent sees how the component is actually used. Maps to agent-ready: real content.

codeConnect.description: The bridge from this contract to the real implementation, and the mapping between described props and code props. Maps to agent-ready: the Code Connect bridge.

implementation.description: Path to the component source, e.g. './Button.tsx'.

propMap.description: Contract prop name to code prop name.

agentNotes.description: Optional free-text guidance to the agent that does not fit the structured fields.
